newsitem.title: USA: Senate majority leader says U.S. not "world nanny".
newsitem.headline: Senate majority leader says U.S. not "world nanny".

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Sunday the United States cannot be the "world nanny" and that he had opposed the initial deployment of U.S. troops to Bosnia.

"I voted against putting the troops in Bosnia for a variety of reasons, one of them, I never believed they'd only be there one year," the Republican from Mississippi said on ABC Television's "This Week."
"And now in fact the president is saying, 'well yes it's not going to be a year, it's going to be like another year and a half'," Lott said.

Before leaving on his 12-day trip, President Bill Clinton announced he had agreed to commit 8,500 U.S. ground troops to participate in a new NATO mission aimed at fostering the peace accords in Bosnia. The current peacekeeping mission, which has involved about 20,000 U.S. forces in Bosnia for the past year, would be withdrawn.
Clinton indicated the cost would be about $1 billion and if the United States were to commit troops for both Bosnia and Zaire the cost could exceed $3 billion, Lott said.

"I want to make sure what our mission is, why haven't the deadlines of the Dayton accords been complied with?" Lott said. "We cannot be the world nanny. But we do have certain responsibilities and occasions where we clearly can be helpful and that we should take advantage of," he said.
On Zaire, Lott said, "it's not clear really what we're gonna do, what we should do, but when you have that kind of human suffering, if we can be of assistance in a logistic way, I would prefer that."
